title: GDPR data-subject rights
why: The GDPR grants rights that a generic retention rule cannot satisfy: lawful basis, access and portability, erasure, restriction, and a record of processing. Each is a separate obligation with its own failure mode.

addRequirements.title: Every purpose has a recorded lawful basis
addRequirements.statement: When personal data is processed, the application shall record the lawful basis and the purpose for that processing.
addRequirements.definition: Each field a {secondary} supplies is held for a named purpose with a named legal basis, not for "the product" in general.
addRequirements.failurePath: If a purpose has no basis recorded, the write is refused rather than accepted under an implied consent.
acceptance: Given a field with no recorded basis, when it is written, then the write is refused with a stable code.
Given the processing record, when it is exported, then each purpose names its basis and the data it covers.

addRequirements.title: A subject can obtain their data in a portable form
addRequirements.statement: When a data subject requests their data, the application shall produce a machine-readable export of everything held about them through an auditable request path.
addRequirements.definition: One request produces one complete file, and the {secondary} can tell which request produced it.
addRequirements.failurePath: If the export would omit a store the product knows about, the request fails loudly instead of returning a plausible partial file.
acceptance: Given a subject with records in every store, when they request an export, then each store's records appear in the file.
Given an export, when it is requested a second time, then the request is recorded and the file reflects current data.

addRequirements.title: Erasure removes the data and records that it did
addRequirements.statement: When a subject requests erasure and no legal hold applies, the application shall remove their personal data from primary storage, derived stores and caches.
addRequirements.definition: After erasure a search for the subject returns nothing except the non-personal audit of the erasure itself.
addRequirements.failurePath: If a legal hold applies, the request is refused with the reason and the hold's end condition, never silently ignored.
acceptance: Given a subject with a legal hold, when erasure is requested, then it is refused with the hold named.
Given an accepted erasure, when every store is queried, then no personal field remains and the audit entry survives.

addRequirements.title: A processing register is generated, not hand-written
addRequirements.statement: The repository shall contain a processing register that lists each purpose, its basis, the data categories, the recipients and the retention period.
addRequirements.definition: The register is a build artifact with a test, not a document someone remembers to update.
addRequirements.failurePath: If the register omits a purpose the code processes, the check fails rather than publishing an incomplete record.
acceptance: Given a new purpose in code, when the register is not updated, then the check fails and names the purpose.
Given the register, when it is exported, then every entry names basis, categories, recipients and retention.

addGates.statement: Access and erasure are both exercised by a test against every store the product owns.
